name: Titanium.UI.ScrollableView
summary:
A view that encapsulates a horizontally-scrolling set of child views, known as pages, navigable
using its built-in horizontal swipe gestures.
description:
| Android | iOS |
| ------- | --- |
| ![Android](./scrollableview_android.png) |  |

Use the [Titanium.UI.createScrollableView](api:Titanium.UI#createScrollableView) method or **`<ScrollableView>`** Alloy element to create
a scrollable view.

The `ScrollableView` supports an on-screen paging control to indicate whether a previous or next
page exists. When the paging control is enabled on iOS, by default it appears as
small dots on the bottom of the screen, whereas Android displays arrows on the left and
right-hand sides.

Use the `cacheSize` property to cache views inside the scrollable view. This can be required when
using complex view structures in the scrollable view (e.g. map views) and the app might crash if no
proper cache size is specified. See the [Titanium.UI.ScrollableView.cacheSize](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#cacheSize) documentation for more
infos regarding view caching.

Only the `scroll` event exists for the `ScrollableView` on Android. To support others, child
views may be added to pages, and event listeners added to these views instead of the pages
themselves.

In a previous Titanium version for iOS, the `maxZoomScale` and `minZoomScale` properties were
removed for performance and parity reasons. As they still remain in [Titanium.UI.ScrollView](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollView),
the equivalent functionality may be obtained by adding a `ScrollView` to `ScrollableView`. See
the "Simple Scrollable View with 2 Zoomable Images" example for a demonstration.

examples.title: Simple Scrollable View with 3 Views
Simple Scrollable View with 2 Zoomable Images
Scrollable View with multiple visible views
Alloy XML Markup
examples.code:
First example as an Alloy view.

``` xml
<Alloy>
    <Window id="win">
        <ScrollableView id="scrollableView" showPagingControl="true">
            <View id="view1" backgroundColor="#123">
              <Label>View 1</Label>
            </View>
            <View id="view2" backgroundColor="#246">
            <Label>View 2</Label>
            </View>
            <View id="view3" backgroundColor="#48b">
            <Label>View 3</Label>
            </View>
        </ScrollableView>
    </Window>
</Alloy>
```

properties.name: cacheSize
properties.summary: Number of pages to cache (pre-render).
properties.description:
Pages are rendered in the range (currentPage +/- (cacheSize - 1)/2), *rounded down* for even
values (i.e. cacheSize=4 renders 3 pages into the cache.) Keep in mind that improved
performance (larger cache) will lead to faster performance, but greater memory usage.

properties.name: clipViews
properties.summary:
Determines whether the previous and next pages are clipped, so that they are not visible
adjacent to the current page.
properties.description:
Set to `false` to allow the previous or next pages to be seen. Note that
ScrollableView's [width](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#width) must be smaller than its parent
view in order to make this property effective on iOS.
For Android you have to set the [padding](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#padding) property.

Check the `Scrollable View with multiple visible views` example for both platforms.

properties.name: currentPage
properties.summary: Index of the active page.
properties.description:
Since Titanium Mobile Release 3.3.0, using this property to change current page changes the
page without animation on iOS and Android.

properties.name: currentPageIndicatorColor
properties.summary: Color for the current page of the paging control, as a color name or hex triplet.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: disableBounce
properties.summary: Determines whether page bouncing effect is disabled.

properties.name: hitRect
properties.summary: Sets the region where this view responds to gestures.
properties.description:
This property is particularly useful when [clipViews](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#clipViews)
is set to `false` and the dimension of this view is small, to create a larger area for the
user to perform swipe gestures against.

Note that the `x` and `y` values specified are relative to the position of the view.

properties.name: overlayEnabled
properties.summary: Determines whether the paging control is added as an overlay to the view.
properties.description:
If this property is set to `true`, the view takes up the entire height available in the
parent view and the paging control is placed over the view. It is advisable to set an
appropriate value for [pagingControlAlpha](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#pagingControlAlpha)
along with this property, so that the underlying view content may be seen properly.

properties.name: overScrollMode
properties.summary: Determines the behavior when the user overscolls the view.

properties.name: padding
properties.summary: The padding applied to the scrollable view.

properties.name: pageIndicatorColor
properties.summary: Color of the paging control, as a color name or hex triplet.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: pagingControlAlpha
properties.summary: Alpha value of the paging control.

properties.name: pagingControlColor
properties.summary: Color of the paging control, as a color name or hex triplet.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: pagingControlHeight
properties.summary: Height of the paging control, in pixels.

properties.name: pagingControlOnTop
properties.summary: Determines whether the paging control is displayed at the top or bottom of the view.
properties.description: Set to `true` for the paging control at the top.

properties.name: pagingControlTimeout
properties.summary: Number of milliseconds to wait before hiding the paging control.
properties.description: Set to less than or equal to `0` to disable timeout, to keep controls displayed.

properties.name: preferredIndicatorImage
properties.summary: The preferred image for indicators, defined using a local filesystem path, or a `Blob` object containing image data.
properties.description:
Symbol images are recommended. Use [Titanium.UI.iOS.systemImage](api:Titanium.UI.iOS#systemImage) to get system-supplied symbol images.
See examples section for usage.

properties.name: scrollingEnabled
properties.summary: Determines whether scrolling is enabled for the view.
properties.description: If this property is unset or `true`, scrolling is enabled.

properties.name: showPagingControl
properties.summary: Determines whether the paging control is visible.
properties.description: Set to `true` to show paging control.

properties.name: views
properties.summary: Sets the pages within this Scrollable View.

methods.name: addView
methods.summary: Adds a new page to this Scrollable View.

methods.name: insertViewsAt
methods.summary: Inserts views at the specified position in the [views](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#views) array.

parameters.name: position
parameters.summary: Position(index) in the [views](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#views) array to insert the view

methods.name: moveNext
methods.summary: Sets the current page to the next consecutive page in [Titanium.UI.ScrollableView.views](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#views).
methods.description: Since Titanium Mobile Release 3.3.0, using this method to change current page animates the change on iOS and Android.

methods.name: movePrevious
methods.summary: Sets the current page to the previous consecutive page in [Titanium.UI.ScrollableView.views](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#views).
methods.description: Since Titanium Mobile Release 3.3.0, using this method to change current page animates the change on iOS and Android.

methods.name: removeView
methods.summary: Removes an existing page from this Scrollable View.
methods.description:
On Android, does nothing if the page does not exist in
[Titanium.UI.ScrollableView.views](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#views).

On iOS, throws an exception if the page does not exist in [Titanium.UI.ScrollableView.views](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#views)
or the index is invalid.

parameters.name: view
parameters.summary:
A [Titanium.UI.View](api:Titanium.UI.View) object (all platforms) or integer index (Android and iOS only) of
the page to remove.

methods.name: scrollToView
methods.summary: Scrolls to the specified page in [Titanium.UI.ScrollableView.views](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#views).

parameters.name: view
parameters.summary: An integer index or [Titanium.UI.View](api:Titanium.UI.View) object to set as the current page.

methods.name: setIndicatorImageForPage
methods.summary: Sets the indicator image for the specified page.
methods.description:
Override the indicator image for a specific page. Symbol images are recommended.
Use [Titanium.UI.iOS.systemImage](api:Titanium.UI.iOS#systemImage) to get system-supplied symbol images. See examples section for usage.

parameters.name: image
parameters.summary:
The image for the indicator, defined using a local filesystem path,
or a `Blob` object containing image data. Resets to the default if image is null.

parameters.name: pageNo
parameters.summary: Page number to set the image.

events.name: longpress
events.summary: Fired when the device detects a long press against this view.
events.description:
Generated by touching and holding on a touchscreen, this event occurs before the
finger is lifted again. Note that `longpress` cannot be generated with a trackball.

properties.name: x
properties.summary: X coordinate of the event from the `source` view's coordinate system.

properties.name: y
properties.summary: Y coordinate of the event from the `source` view's coordinate system.

events.name: scroll
events.summary: Fired repeatedly as the view is being scrolled.
events.description:
Prior to 2.1, the scroll event did not fire consistently on all platforms. On iOS,
it fired when scrolling ended, and on Android, it fired when drag ended. You can restore
the pre-2.1 behavior by listening for the `scrollEnd` or `dragEnd` events instead.

properties.name: currentPage
properties.summary: Index of the currently visible view of [Titanium.UI.ScrollableView.views](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#views).

properties.name: currentPageAsFloat
properties.summary:
Current page index that the view is scrolled to as a float. For
example, if the user is holding the `ScrollableView` in between
the first and second page, this will have a value of 0.5.

properties.name: view
properties.summary: The currently visible view.

events.name: scrollend
events.summary: Fired when the view has stopped moving completely.

properties.name: currentPage
properties.summary: Index of the currently visible view of [Titanium.UI.ScrollableView.views](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView#views).
